samples.summary: Importing a default (non-`--raw`) CSV export writes the neutralized `'=…` text into the *formula* field, corrupting the cell
samples.evidence: `buildCellMapFromTable` uses column 2 unconditionally: `if (formula !== '') { cells[ref] = { formula }; }` — it never routes that text through `toCellPatch`. A default `sheets export` neutralizes the formula column (`formatCsv(..., {neutralizeFormulas: true})` → `'=SUM(B2:B100)`), and `isCellTable` still matches its `ref,value,formula,style` header, so `sheets export out.csv && sheets import out.csv` sends `{ formula: "'=SUM(B2:B100)" }` — an apostrophe-prefixed string stored in the cell's `f` field (cells.controller.ts:171), i.e. a permanently broken formula rather than literal text. `packages/cli/skills/sheets-import-export.md` asserts the opposite ("`'=SUM(...)` starts with `'`, so a neutralized export comes back as literal text") — that is only true of the grid path (`buildCellMap` → `toCellPatch`), which an export never takes. The same root also mutates neutralized *value* cells: `=foo` exported non-raw comes back as the literal text `'=foo`, not `=foo`.

samples.summary: `findOrCreateUser` runs before the new OAuth state validation, so a refused/forged callback still provisions a user account
samples.evidence: `githubAuthCallback` calls `this.userService.findOrCreateUser({...})` at line 115, but the state checks that decide whether the callback is legitimate are at lines 144 (`typeof stateToken !== 'string'`) and 162 (`webOAuthStateMatches`). Every callback that the new guard then refuses — a missing/repeated `state`, a mismatched cookie, an expired CLI state — has already created (or touched) a user row as a side effect. The refusal path is explicitly documented as reachable without an attacker (10-minute cookie, second login tab), so unvalidated DB writes happen on ordinary failures; the validation should precede the write.

samples.summary: Blank exported cells are skipped on re-import, so an export→import round trip cannot clear cells and is not the identity the charter now claims
samples.evidence: `buildCellMapFromTable` emits nothing for a row where both `value` and `formula` are empty (`if (formula !== '') … else if (value !== '') …`). An exported empty cell therefore leaves whatever is already at that ref in the destination tab untouched. `scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md` was updated in this change to assert `sheets import` → `sheets export --raw` is "the same data"; for a non-empty destination tab it is a merge, not a round trip.

samples.summary: `isCellTable` is a header heuristic that hijacks an ordinary user grid whose first three columns are named ref/value/formula
samples.evidence: `isCellTable` returns true for any CSV whose first three trimmed/lowercased header cells are `ref`,`value`,`formula` — including a hand-authored data file about spreadsheet references. Such an import silently ignores `--start` (sheets-import.ts:104-107) and writes rows to the refs named in column 0 instead of the requested block, and rows whose column 0 is not `/^[A-Z]+\d+$/` are dropped entirely (line 120) with no error — a silent partial import. Only the `mode` field in the response hints at it.

samples.summary: Grid CSV import now reinterprets any `=`-leading cell text as a formula, changing existing import behaviour
samples.evidence: `buildCellMap` previously always emitted `{ value }`; it now calls `toCellPatch(value)`, which sends any cell whose text starts with `=` as `{ formula }`. Every existing positional-CSV import that contained literal text beginning with `=` (e.g. `=>`, `=TBD`) now lands in the `f` field and is evaluated/errored by the formula engine instead of being stored verbatim. No opt-out flag exists on the import side (only `--raw` on export).

samples.summary: `--start` is still parsed (and can throw) on the cell-table path where it is documented as inapplicable
samples.evidence: `parseStartRef(localOpts.start)` is called unconditionally at line 104, before the `cellTable ? … : …` branch. An invalid `--start` therefore aborts an import of an exported ref-table with a start-ref error even though the schema and help text now say `--start` is ignored for that input shape.

samples.summary: A malformed `challenge` is dropped silently at login start and only fails after the full GitHub round trip, stranding the CLI
samples.evidence: `parseCliChallenge(req.query?.challenge)` returns `undefined` for anything not exactly 43 base64url chars, and `createState` stores `challenge: undefined`. The failure is not raised until `auth.controller.ts:179-184` throws `BadRequestException` after the user has completed GitHub sign-in. The CLI's loopback server never receives a callback in that case, so `wafflebase login` waits the full `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 s) and then reports the generic timeout with no refusal reason (login.ts:397-403) — the backend's explanatory 400 is only visible in the browser. The same dead end is guaranteed for any pre-PKCE CLI.

samples.summary: `loginErrorUrl` silently produces a host-relative redirect when `FRONTEND_URL` is unset
samples.evidence: `(this.configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL') ?? '')` yields `''`, so the refusal redirects to `/login?error=oauth_state` on the *backend* origin — the very "raw page on the backend origin with no way back" the comment says it exists to avoid. The success path at line 209 uses `configService.get('FRONTEND_URL')!` and would fail loudly instead; the two disagree about whether the value can be absent.

samples.summary: Spreading the server response after `mode` lets the server silently override the locally computed `mode`/`imported` fields
samples.evidence: `{ imported: cellCount, mode, ...res.data as Record<string, unknown> }` — if the batch endpoint ever returns an `imported` or `mode` key, the caller-visible values documented in the schema registry (`'cells' | 'grid'`) are replaced by the server's. The new `mode` field is the only signal that `--start` was ignored, so overriding it is a correctness-relevant loss.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. buildCellMapFromTable (packages/cli/src/util/csv-parse.ts:121-130) assigns row[2] directly as `{ formula }` without passing it through toCellPatch (csv-parse.ts:90-92). A default `sheets export` sets neutralizeFormulas: true (sheets-export.ts:63), and formatCsv neutralizes every field including the formula column (csv.ts:91 -> neutralizeFormula csv.ts:33-42), emitting `'=SUM(B2:B100)`. The export payload keys are ref,value,formula,style (backend cells.controller.ts:60-65), so isCellTable still matches (csv-parse.ts:103-107) and sheets-import.ts:103-107 takes the table path. The apostrophe-prefixed text is then stored verbatim in the cell's `f` field (cells.controller.ts:168-171), producing a permanently broken formula rather than the literal text the skill doc promises (skills/sheets-import-export.md:110-114). The existing test only exercises the --raw shape (test/csv-parse.test.ts:143-160), so nothing contradicts this. No guard elsewhere strips the neutralizing quote. Real, reachable data corruption on the default export->import flow; in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: The ordering the reviewer describes is real (findOrCreateUser at auth.controller.ts:115 precedes the state checks at :144 and :162), but it is not a blocking defect under the Correctness rubric. (a) The "forged callback" premise is gated: @UseGuards(AuthGuard('github')) at auth.controller.ts:107 completes the GitHub code/token/profile exchange before the handler body runs (github.strategy.ts:70-81), so only GitHub-verified identities reach line 115. (b) The write is idempotent and non-destructive: user.service.ts:40-48 returns any existing row unmodified and only creates when the unique email is unseen, so the benign refusal paths (:144-146, :162-164) create exactly the row the user's own retry would create, and the retry reuses it — no data loss, no overwrite, no crash, and no session is issued on any refusal path (createTokens is only reached at :206). (c) There is no amplification: creation is keyed to a unique GitHub-verified email, so no actor can provision anything they could not provision via a normal successful login. What is left is validation-ordering hardening for a login-CSRF defense, which belongs to the Security lens explicitly excluded from this lane; there is no wrong condition, boundary error, missing-guard crash, async/race mistake, or observably broken invariant.
